items.label: ✓ Found the right person

items.label: ✓ Rightly refused: not this person
items.value: The card and the person don't agree, so nobody should be returned. The matcher refused (HRex 422).

items.label: ✓ Rightly refused: can't tell apart
items.value: More than one member fits the request equally. HRex says refuse (422), and the matcher did.

items.label: ✓ Rightly refused: consent
items.value: The consent sent with the request can't be honoured, so HRex says refuse (422). The matcher did.

items.label: ✗ Wrong person
items.value: The matcher returned a member who is not the person asking, or returned someone when it should have refused. This is how one person's records reach another.

items.label: ✗ Ignored consent
items.value: The matcher returned the right person despite a consent the plan can't honour.

items.label: ✗ Missed the right person
items.value: One member was the right answer, but the matcher refused. Safe, but the member's records don't move.

items.label: ✗ No usable answer
items.value: The matcher crashed or answered in a form that isn't a valid $member-match response.

rationales.rationale: The demographics, member ID (SYN-MEM-1001-01) and subscriber ID (SYN-SUB-1001) all agree on a single member, John Roe, born 1951-09-02. The Consent is active and covers today (2026-11-01), within 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30. Its policy URI points to the HRex 'sensitive' policy, which requires the payer to segment sensitive data. The payer's canSegmentSensitiveData is false, so it cannot comply with the consent terms. The required answer is a 422 consent failure, and no member ID is returned.

Name, gender, birthDate (2008-07-01) and subscriberId SYN-SUB-2001 all point to a single roster member, SYN-MEM-2001-02 (Rowan Quill Jr). The request has no suffix, but the birthDate separates him from Rowan Sr. The Consent is active, in period on 2026-11-01, and names the patient as performer (he is 18). Its policy is the '#sensitive' one, which covers disclosure of sensitive data. The payer has canSegmentSensitiveData=false and cannot honor that consent, so under HRex it must return 422 for the consent rather than a match.

The subscriber ID SYN-SUB-2001, family name Quill, gender female and birth date 2012-05-20 all agree with two dependents, Ada (SYN-MEM-2001-03) and Aya (SYN-MEM-2001-04). The request gives only the initial "A" as the given name, which fits both, and the coverage relationship is data-absent "unknown", so nothing separates them. The Consent is active and within its period (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30). It permits disclosure including sensitive data, so the payer's inability to segment sensitive data does not stop it from complying. Because more than one member fits and they cannot be told apart, the answer is a 422 multiple-matches refusal.

Name, birth date, gender, member ID and subscriber ID all agree with SYN-MEM-1001-01 (John Roe, 1951-09-02). The near-duplicate Jon Roe (1951-09-10) has different IDs and birth date, so identity is not in doubt. However, the request includes a Consent that cannot be honored. Its policy is the HRex sensitive-data policy, and the payer cannot segment sensitive data. The permit period (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31) also ended before today (2026-11-01). Because the payer cannot comply with the consent, it must return 422 and not a match.

The Coverage member id (SYN-MEM-1001-01) and subscriber id (SYN-SUB-1001) both point to the same roster member. The name John Roe, birth date 1951-09-02 and gender male also agree. The similar roster entry Jon Roe has a different member id, subscriber id and birth date, so it is not a candidate. The Consent is active and permits disclosure, with a period (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30) that covers today (2026-11-01). It contains no sensitive-data restrictions, so the payer's inability to segment sensitive data does not stop it from complying.

The demographics (John Roe, male, 1951-09-02) match SYN-MEM-1001-01 exactly. The Coverage member ID (SYN-MEM-1002-01) and subscriber ID (SYN-SUB-1002) point to a different member, Jon Roe, born 1951-09-10. Because the two sets of identifiers name two different people, I cannot safely return either one, and a human must resolve the conflict. The active Consent also carries a sensitive-data policy that this payer cannot honor because canSegmentSensitiveData is false, so no data could be released on this request in any case.
